title: Telemetry Compatibility Escrow and Consumer Isolation Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the Telemetry Compatibility Escrow (TCE) process and the end-to-end operator guidance for consumer isolation. It codifies a predictable escrow window for backward-compatible signal migration, automated compatibility checks, canary rollout patterns for telemetry schema changes, and fast rollback procedures for downstream consumer faults. The goal is to keep runtime observability stable during platform evolution while giving consumers time and tools to migrate without causing incident noise or SLO regressions.

Why we need a compatibility escrow:
- Telemetry schema and signal changes are frequent (new tags, renamed fields, sampling changes).
- Uncoordinated changes cause consumer failures, alert storms, and misattributed SLI burn.
- Platform teams must be able to evolve signals while guaranteeing a bounded operational risk window for consumers.

Scope and definitions:
- Telemetry signal: any event, metric, span, log, or derived artifact emitted by platform services.
- Producer: the service/SDK releasing telemetry changes (e.g., runtime, allocator, platform-sidecar).
- Consumer: dashboards, alerting rules, billing pipelines, ML quality monitors, and downstream services pulling telemetry.
- Compatibility escrow window: the minimum time a producer must support the old signal form while the new form is available (default 14 days).
- Adapter: lightweight mapping layer that converts between old and new signal schemas for consumers during escrow.

Principles:
1) Backwards-first: new signals must be additive or mark-breaking explicitly; producers own the compatibility cost.
2) Observable canaries: every signal change must ship with a canary plan and observability targets.
3) Consumer-first rollback: if consumer SLIs degrade, automatically prioritize consumer remediation or rollback.
4) Short, enforced escrow: default escrow is 14 days but can be extended with documented approval.
5) Automation over manual: CI gates, contract tests, and rollout orchestration should minimize manual coordination.

Roles and ownership:
- Producer owner (code owner of the emitting service): defines change, writes contract, owns unit tests and adapter implementation.
- Telemetry steward (platform observability team): validates contract tests, runs compatibility CI, and approves escrow end.
- Consumer liaisons (owners of major dashboards/alerts/pipelines): sign off on rollback triggers and are notified of canaries.
- Oncall (platform SRE): monitors canary dashboards and triggers rollback if thresholds crossed.

SLOs and alert thresholds during escrow:
- Canary success criteria (default 72-hour window):
  - No >20% increase in missing-signal rate for critical dashboards.
  - No >10% increase in false-positive alert rate for token-cost or SLO-burn alerts.
  - Consumer ingestion error rate < 0.5% sustained per-host over 1h.
- Escrow safety SLOs:
  - Escrow observability: all adapters must expose a telemetry_escrow.status metric (OK/WARN/FAIL).
  - Rollback SLA: platform SRE must acknowledge and trigger rollback within 30 minutes of safety SLO violation.

Process: high-level steps (producer perspective)
1) Draft change and contract:
   - Document change in the PR: reason, schema diff, mapping example, affected consumers, escrow window request.
   - Add a compatibility.json contract under telemetry/contracts/<service>/<change-id>.json.
2) Implement dual-write and adapter:
   - Emit both old and new signal formats (dual-write) behind a feature flag for the escrow window OR ship a producer-side adapter that provides the old schema to consumers.
   - Add metrics: telemetry_escrow.dual_write.enabled (boolean), telemetry_escrow.adapter.errors (count).
3) CI and contract tests:
   - Run automated contract tests (see CI snippet below).
   - Ensure at least two consumer regression tests pass in the compatibility CI matrix.
4) Canary rollout (see canary plan):
   - Start in region us-west-2 to limit blast radius.
   - Monitor canary dashboards for 72 hours.
5) Notify consumers and open migration ticket:
   - Create a public migration ticket in the platform tracker and tag consumer teams.
6) End of escrow:
   - Telemetry steward validates signals and approves removal of old format after escrow window and when adapter error rate = 0 for 48h.

Operator runbook: canary and rollback (step-by-step)
1) Pre-canary checklist (producer + steward):
   - Contract file present and validated by CI.
   - Canary dashboard created from template: telemetry/canary-templates/<service>-schema-change.
   - Alert rules created for missing-signal-rate and adapter-error-rate.
   - Escrow ticket published with consumer contact list.
2) Start canary:
   - Flip feature flag to enable new-write for 1% of hosts in canary cohort (or enable adapter in read-path).
   - Observe telemetry_escrow.metrics for immediate errors.
3) Operator monitoring (first 4 hours intensive):
   - Check: missing-signal-rate, ingestion-error-rate, SLO burn for key dashboards.
   - If any threshold breached, mark incident and follow rollback.
4) Rollback procedure (fast path):
   - Toggle feature flag off OR re-enable adapter routing to old format.
   - Post-rollback: run a short regression test suite, notify affected consumers, and open postmortem if rollback invoked.
5) Slow rollback (consumer remediation):
   - If consumer teams request more time, extend escrow by documented approval. Add a compensating adapter if needed.

CI contract test example (YAML):
- name: telemetry-compatibility-check
  steps:
    - run: python telemetry_contracts/validate_contract.py --contract telemetry/contracts/runtime/2026-02-schema-change.json
    - run: python telemetry_contracts/run_consumer_smoke.py --consumer-list core-dashboards,billing-pipeline
    - run: bash ./scripts/check_adapter_health.sh

Compatibility test expectations:
- Schema diffs are validated (added fields allowed, renamed fields must provide alias mapping).
- Consumer smoke tests verify alert rules and downstream queries still return values within tolerance.

Adapter patterns and examples:
- Producer-side adapter: a small service that accepts new-format events and republishes old-format events to the internal topic. Lightweight and recommended when dual-write is expensive.
- Consumer-side shim: library packages consumers can opt into to accept both formats (recommended for internal dashboards).
- Example adapter mapping (JSON):
  {
    "old_event_type": "llm.request",
    "new_event_type": "llm.request.v2",
    "mappings": {
      "req_id": "id",
      "prompt.text": "input.prompt",
      "tokens.total": "cost.tokens"
    }
  }

Dashboards and alerting templates (what to create)
- Canary dashboard: 4 panels (missing-signal-rate, adapter-errors, consumer-ingest-latency, SLI-burn-heatmap).
- Alerts:
  - Missing-signal-rate > 15% for 10m -> P1 notify platform-oncall and page producer owner.
  - Adapter errors > 0.5% sustained for 30m -> P1.
  - Consumer ingestion error rate > 0.5% per-host 1h -> P2 (investigate).

Escrow policy matrix (table-like text)
Change type | Minimum escrow | Notes
Additive field | 3 days | Safe, consumers ignore unknown fields
Renamed field w/ alias | 14 days | Producer must provide alias mapping and adapter
Semantic change (units/scale) | 28 days | Requires both dual-write and consumer regression verification
Signal removal | 28+ days and approval | Must be announced in migration tracker and have adapters available

Escrow enforcement and automation:
- The telemetry steward runs a daily job that lists all open escrow tickets and flags any that are past-window for follow-up.
- CI enforces that any PR changing telemetry must reference a contract ID and escrow window. Missing metadata blocks merge.
- A small automated adapter-generator tool (telemetry/adapter-gen) can scaffold adapters from mapping files to speed producer work.

Training and handoff:
- Operator playbook training: 90-minute lab covering a sample schema change, canary dashboard interpretation, and rollback drills.
- Simulation cadence: quarterly simulated telemetry-schema-failure gameday with at least two consumer teams participating.

FAQ (short)
Q: What if a consumer is third-party and cannot modify quickly?
A: Producers must provide an adapter for the third-party or prolong escrow after written approval from the telemetry steward and security review.

Q: Can consumers opt out of escrow?
A: No — escrow is platform-level governance; consumers can request an extended contract for dedicated signals.

References and templates:
- Contract template: telemetry/contracts/template-schema-change.md
- Canary dashboard template: telemetry/canary-templates/schema-change-basic.jsonnet
- Adapter generator: //git/internal/telemetry/adapter-gen README

Appendix: emergency rollback checklist (operator oncall)
1) Acknowledge page and escalate to producer owner.
2) Capture snapshot of canary dashboard (panels listed above).
3) Follow fast rollback toggle (feature flag steps included in the PR).
4) Post-rollback run: consumer smoke tests, mark escrow ticket with rollback reason, create incident if service impact > 5% SLI burn.

Contact and escalation
- Telemetry steward rotation: observability-team@redwood.com
- Platform SRE oncall: platform-oncall@pagerduty (page immediately for P1)
- Producer owner: listed on each escrow ticket
